title: Legacy Logistics Integration
business: A modern e-commerce platform transitioning to a microservices architecture.
problem: The new order management system must integrate with a legacy mainframe logistics provider that uses proprietary, rigid data formats, threatening to pollute the clean domain model of the new system with legacy constraints.
solution: An Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) acts as a protective boundary, translating the legacy system's complex, non-standard data structures into the clean, domain-specific objects required by the new order management system.
steps: Define a clean domain interface that represents the order requirements without legacy baggage.
Implement a facade or adapter that communicates with the legacy logistics API.
Create a translation layer that maps legacy data fields into the domain objects.
Route all interactions through the translation layer so the domain model remains isolated from the legacy system.
outcome: The core domain model remains decoupled from the legacy system, allowing for easier future migrations or replacements of the logistics provider.
limitation: The ACL introduces a maintenance overhead because any change in the legacy system's schema requires a corresponding update to the translation logic, which can be verified by monitoring the mapping layer's unit test coverage.

questions.question: In Legacy Logistics Integration, what is the primary purpose of the Anti-Corruption Layer?
options: To replace the legacy mainframe entirely.
To protect the domain model from legacy data constraints.
To increase the performance of the legacy database.
To provide a user interface for the logistics team.
questions.explanation: The ACL is designed to prevent legacy system structures from polluting the clean domain model.
questions.evidence: An Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) acts as a protective boundary, translating the legacy system's complex, non-standard data structures into the clean, domain-specific objects required by the new order management system.

questions.question: In Legacy Logistics Integration, what is a key limitation of implementing an ACL?
options: It prevents the system from ever connecting to new services.
It requires the legacy system to be rewritten first.
It creates maintenance overhead when the legacy schema changes.
It forces the domain model to use legacy data types.
questions.explanation: The translation logic must be updated whenever the underlying legacy system changes, creating an ongoing maintenance task.
questions.evidence: The ACL introduces a maintenance overhead because any change in the legacy system's schema requires a corresponding update to the translation logic, which can be verified by monitoring the mapping layer's unit test coverage.
